subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Which channel/source delivery policy should close this issue: a guarded final/message-tool-only safety policy for tool-using turns, opt-in mitigations only, or a narrower cron/substrate fix first?
rationale: The safest fix touches user-visible delivery defaults and can intentionally suppress replies that existing deployments may expect, so automation should not choose the permanent compatibility/security tradeoff alone.

options.title: Adopt guarded channel-safety policy
options.body: Treat bare inter-tool assistant text as private for channel/source turns and require migration or fallback proof for users who rely on automatic bare-text replies.

options.title: Ship opt-in mitigations only
options.body: Land mitigations such as final-tag enforcement or verbose-off suppression while keeping automatic source delivery as the default compatibility path.

options.title: Fix cron/substrate first
options.body: Land the narrow reasoning-metadata and NO_REPLY substrate repairs, then leave the direct/source default decision open for a later maintainer call.

recommendation.title: Adopt guarded channel-safety policy
recommendation.body: Treat bare inter-tool assistant text as private for channel/source turns and require migration or fallback proof for users who rely on automatic bare-text replies.
